title: Maximum Subarray

statement.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum, and return that sum.
statement.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
statement.outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum subarray sum.
statement.notes: The array may contain negative numbers.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum = 6.

hints: Kadane's algorithm: track the best sum ending at the current index, reset it to the current element if it drops below that.
Watch the all-negative case — the answer must include at least one element.

editorial.text: Maintain `currentSum` and `maxSum`. At each element, currentSum = max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i]); maxSum = max(maxSum, currentSum).

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence

statement.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
statement.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
statement.outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the LIS.
statement.notes: A subsequence need not be contiguous.

hints: O(n^2) DP works but won't scale for large n — think O(n log n) with binary search.

editorial.text: Maintain a `tails` array where tails[i] is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length i+1. Binary search for the position to replace on each element.

title: Watermelon Split

statement.description: You are given an integer weight `w` of a watermelon. Determine whether it's possible to split it into two parts, each with a positive even weight, summing to `w`.
statement.notes: Read input from stdin, write output to stdout.

examples.explanation: 3 is odd, can't split into two even parts.

hints: Even weight ≥ 4 can always be split into two positive even parts.

editorial.text: w works if and only if w is even and w > 2.

title: Shortest Path in Weighted Graph

statement.description: Given a weighted, undirected graph with `n` nodes and `m` edges, find the shortest distance from node 1 to node n.
statement.inputFormat:
First line: n, m.
Next m lines: u, v, w (edge between u and v with weight w).
statement.outputFormat: A single integer — shortest distance, or -1 if unreachable.

examples.explanation: Path 1→2→3→4 costs 1+2+1 = 4, cheaper than direct edge (10).

hints: Use Dijkstra's algorithm with a priority queue for O((n+m) log n).
Watch out for disconnected graphs — return -1 if node n is unreachable.

editorial.text: Standard Dijkstra with a min-heap. Track visited nodes and shortest known distances; relax edges as you pop from the heap.

title: Two Sum

statement.description: Given an array of integers and a target value, find two distinct indices whose values add up to the target. Return the indices of the two elements.
statement.inputFormat: First line: n, target. Second line: n integers representing the array.
statement.outputFormat: Print two distinct indices whose values sum to target. If no such pair exists, print -1.
statement.notes: Indices are 0-based. It is guaranteed that at most one valid pair exists.

examples.explanation: The elements at indices 0 and 1 are 2 and 7, and 2 + 7 = 9.
No two distinct elements have a sum of 10.

hints: For each number, check whether its complement has already appeared.
A hash map can reduce the solution from O(n²) to O(n).

editorial.text: Store previously seen values and their indices in a hash map. For each value x, check whether target - x has already been seen.

title: Maximum Subarray

statement.description: Given an array of integers, find the maximum possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
statement.inputFormat: First line: n. Second line: n integers representing the array.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum possible subarray sum.
statement.notes: The subarray must contain at least one element.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the maximum sum: 6.
When every value is negative, the best subarray contains the largest single value.

hints: Keep track of the best sum ending at the current position.
If the previous running sum becomes harmful, start a new subarray.

editorial.text: Use Kadane's algorithm. Maintain the maximum subarray sum ending at each position and update the global maximum.

title: Valid Parentheses

statement.description: Given a string containing only the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine whether the brackets are properly matched and nested.
statement.inputFormat: A single line containing the bracket string.
statement.outputFormat: Print "YES" if the string is valid, otherwise print "NO".
statement.notes: An empty string is considered valid.

examples.explanation: Every opening bracket is correctly matched with its corresponding closing bracket.

hints: Use a stack to remember the opening brackets.
When a closing bracket appears, it must match the most recent opening bracket.

editorial.text: Push every opening bracket onto a stack. For each closing bracket, check that it matches the stack's top element. The stack must be empty after processing the entire string.

title: Counting Connected Components

statement.description: Given an undirected graph with n vertices and m edges, determine the number of connected components in the graph.
statement.inputFormat: First line: n, m. Next m lines: u, v representing an undirected edge between vertices u and v.
statement.outputFormat: Print the number of connected components.
statement.notes: Vertices are numbered from 1 to n. Multiple edges between the same pair of vertices may not appear.

examples.explanation: Vertices 1, 2, 3 form one component and vertices 4, 5 form another.
With no edges, every vertex is an independent component.

hints: Build an adjacency list for the graph.
Start a DFS or BFS from every unvisited vertex and count how many searches are started.

editorial.text: Traverse the graph using DFS or BFS. Every time an unvisited vertex is found, start a new traversal and increment the component count.

title: Range Sum Queries

statement.description: You are given an array of n integers and q queries. For each query [l, r], find the sum of all elements from index l through index r inclusive.
statement.inputFormat: First line: n, q. Second line: n integers. Next q lines: l, r.
statement.outputFormat: For each query, print the sum of the requested range on a separate line.
statement.notes: Indices are 0-based and each query satisfies 0 ≤ l ≤ r < n.

examples.explanation: The three ranges have sums 1+2+3 = 6, 2+3+4 = 9, and 3+4+5 = 12.

hints: Computing every query directly can be too slow.
Build a prefix sum array so each range can be answered in O(1).

editorial.text: Construct a prefix sum array where prefix[i] stores the sum of the first i elements. Each query [l, r] is then answered as prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l].
